root_cause: CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race (caching_test.cpp, TEST_P starting at line 2644) is a stress/race test that repeatedly loads a MULTI-device model through ov::Core for ~2000ms per iteration, asserting mockPlugin->import_model(istream&, ...) is called devCount-1 times per iteration (devCount = 1 + index % 9, cycling 1..9 mock devices). Because the loop duration is wall-clock bounded rather than iteration-count bounded, and each iteration spins up threads to compile/import a model concurrently per device, a slow Windows CI runner can leave the last iteration's import_model calls still in flight (one call 'unsatisfied and active') when TearDown() verifies expectations via Mock::VerifyAndClearExpectations, right after the 2000ms deadline is hit mid-iteration. This is a known timing-sensitive test design (the file's own comment notes 'In case of sporadic failures - increase TEST_DURATION_MS 100x times for better reproducibility'), not a regression introduced by this commit; the triggering commit (#39941, SYCL enqueue_marker barrier fix for the GPU plugin) is unrelated to CPU/inference caching code.
reproduction_steps: Build ieFuncTests on Windows (Release) and run repeatedly under load: `ieFuncTests.exe --gtest_filter=CachingTest/CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race*`. Reproduction is intermittent and more likely on loaded/slower runners; running several times or under CPU contention increases odds of hitting the race window.
recommended_actions: Change the loop's stopping condition in LoadMulti_race/LoadMultiWithConfig_race (src/inference/tests/functional/caching_test.cpp, ~lines 2600-2685) to finish the in-flight iteration fully (check the time budget only between iterations, not relying on TearDown() to catch a still-running iteration) or add a short grace/join wait before the loop exits so async import_model calls complete before Mock verification.

Consider marking this test as flaky-tolerant in CI (e.g., gtest retry/rerun-on-failure) given its documented non-determinism, rather than failing the whole post-commit pipeline on a single sporadic miscount.
No action needed on the triggering PR #39941 (GPU SYCL barrier fix) - it does not touch caching_test.cpp or MULTI/inference caching code.
prevention_strategies: Avoid designing unit tests around hard wall-clock loop deadlines combined with asynchronous mock expectations; prefer deterministic iteration counts or explicit synchronization (e.g., wait for all pending import_model futures before the loop's time check) so TearDown() never races with in-flight async calls.
historical_context: This exact signature has recurred at least twice before this run (2026-11-09 and 2026-11-10, pattern 9f9ea52f699d8da3), both on Windows C++ unit tests jobs with the same import_model call-count mismatch in LoadMultiWithConfig_race. This is the third occurrence; the test's own source comment acknowledges sporadic failures are expected and suggests increasing TEST_DURATION_MS as a workaround, but no fix has been applied yet.
